artists.biography: A doomy stoner metal Pink Floyd tribute project spearheaded by Austin, Texas-based Sword guitarist Kyle Shutt, the aptly named Doom Side of the Moon began in early 2017 as a salute to the 50th anniversary of the legendary English psych/classic rock outfit. Comprising Shutt, fellow Sword-mates bassist Bryan Richie and drummer Santiago Vela III, vocalist Alex Marrero (Brownout, Brown Sabbath), saxophonist Jason Frey (Black Joe Lewis, Hard Proof), and keyboardist Joe Cornetti (Croy & the Boys), the band released its eponymous debut, a complete reworking of Pink Floyd's seminal 1973 classic Dark Side of the Moon, in August 2017. perplexity.description:
Doom Side of the Moon is a heavy metal tribute album released in 2017 by Doom Side of the Moon, a project led by Kyle Shutt, guitarist of The Sword. The album reimagines Pink Floyd’s iconic 1973 progressive rock masterpiece The Dark Side of the Moon through a doom metal lens, transforming its atmospheric textures and melodic subtleties into weighty riffs, distorted guitars, and a darker, more aggressive sonic palette. The arrangements remain faithful to the original track sequence and structure, but the reinterpretation emphasizes slow tempos, heavy grooves, and a sense of brooding intensity characteristic of the doom metal genre.

As a standalone release, Doom Side of the Moon stands apart from Shutt’s work with The Sword, showcasing his appreciation for classic rock and his willingness to experiment with genre reinterpretation. The album was released on Music Theories Recordings and received mixed critical reception. While some reviewers praised its ambition and the novelty of translating Pink Floyd’s work into a doom metal context, others found the arrangements unimaginative and lacking in creative reinterpretation. Commercially, the album found a niche audience among fans of both Pink Floyd and doom metal, but it did not achieve mainstream success.
